THE ACADEMIC WIND OCTET
OF CARACAS
Was formed in February of 1979 by Venezuela's finest wind players.
Its international credits include performances on many of the world's
most distinguished
venues
such as: The Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, The Smithsonian Institution, The Metropolitan Museum of Art
in New York City. They have also performed in Spain, Italy, Uruguay, Argentina, Colombia, Costa Rica,
Chile, Curacao, El Salvador, Jamaica, Mexico and Suriname.
Its large repertoire includes original works by Hayden, Mozart, Beethoven,
and many other celebrated composers. One of the Octet's special features is its unique interpretation
of popular Latin American themes as well as Caribbean music with extraordinary
arrangements done by the most highly regarded musicians from Latin America.

Description
The "Raul Borges"
Trio represents a tradition that goes back several decades to its creation
in 1945. Founded by Antonio Lauro, Flaminia de De Sola and Manual Enrique
Pérez Díaz, three Venezuelan guitar masters united by a common artistic
filiations, they form this prestigious group that takes the name to honor
the memory of a great musician, "Raul Borges", founder of the
Venezuelan School of Classic Guitar (1932) and whose personality is the
starting point for the present generation of Venezuelan guitarists.
In 1985 the group was reactivated through initiative of Antonio Lauro who
chose from his present disciples those who could lend continuity and
enrich the group with equal or greater artistic maturity. At present, The
"Raul Borges" Trio is made up of three excellent Venezuelan
guitarists whose names are Lorenzo Camejo, Alberto Espinoza and José Luis
Presa.

Biography
Julio D'Escriván is a composer, sound designer and music producer. He has a doctorate (Ph.D., TCU 1991) in Electroacoustic Composition from The City University, London where he studied under Simon Emmerson and, occasionally, Robert Saxton. Also a guitarist with an interest in both classical, ethnic and popular music having studied with Chris Kilvington and Nigel St. Clair Morgan and obtained his LGSM (guitar teaching) in 1984. For his undergraduate music education he attended Anglia Polytechnic University, and was taught composition by John Hopkins. Other influential teachers include Peter Britton and Bob Reeve. He took classes with Robin Holloway at Cambridge for one year before going to City University to work on his doctorate.
He has released 3 commercially available records: "Cantos y Tonadas" (1997), Venezuelan music arranged and played with instruments from other ethnic backgrounds .
"VOX" (1998) which features the electroacoustic intervention of the human voice, incorporating pre-Columbian dialects found in Venezuela), and finally
"Inventos Bárbaros" (1999) which deals with music for TV and for the stage.
Julio D'Escriván is currently living and working in Caracas, Venezuela and preparing a new body of work under his own label, Bongo Musique
Editora.

Biography
Andrés Briceño started on percussion at the early age of four with the
guidance of his father, Napoleón Baltodano, a soloist trumpet
player of several Central American orchestras, and was one of the first
jazz improvisers in Venezuela.
Self taught drummer,
Andrés has played with many artists in different musical
styles. His roots led him to study the afro-Venezuelan rhythms. His main
interest has been focused on adapting the Afro-Venezuelan folkloric
drums and percussion rhythms to the drum set, an invader
instrument in Venezuelan folklore music.

Biography
André Carrasquero is a
pianist, arranger, composer and producer born in Montréal and raised in
Caracas, Venezuela.
He began his career as a studio musician in 1983. This eventually led
him to become a producer for other artists as well as for himself, as
well as a composer for film and tv. In 1994, his album Tudo
Brasil was nominated for the 1994 'Premio Casa del Artista' as best
independent production.
Throughout the 1990s,
Carrasquero performed in all major Jazz Festivals in Venezuela with the
"André Carrasquero Trio", the "Solera Jazz Band", and the "Tudo Brasil
Band". He shared the stage with many legendary musicians, including
Arturo Sandoval, Eddie Daniels, and Nestor Torres.
In 1998, André returned to his country of birth, Canada and became very
active in the local music scene. André was the driving force behind the
highly acclaimed Afro Cuban jazz group 'Zapato Negro'.
Their 'Live at the Cellar Jazz' album was nominated for outstanding Jazz
Recording of the year (2007) by the West Coast Music Awards.
In 2004 Carrasquero produced Latin Roots, the first solo album of
international singer/songwriter Susana Williams. In 2021 he co-produced
her second solo album "We're A Memory." He is currently the music
director of Williams' Latin Jazz quartet headlining at such venues like
the "Shadbolt Centre", the "Gibsons Landing Jazz Festival" and the
legendary "Frankie's Jazz Club"..

spending nearly all his free time practicing. Later
on he studied at the University of Miami, where he received a master's
degree in jazz. . Ed Calle has been involved
on a lot of recordings both as a sideman and a soloist, and his resume

Gonzalo
Micó

Caracas, Venezuela
Guitar, Steel Pan
Jazz
Biography
Gonzalo
Micó is one of the top guitar virtuosos in Venezuela and, for many years, one of the few pillars of the Venezuelan Jazz scene.
He schooled under Profesor Joe Diorio and learned composition under Carl Schoroeder and graduated from the Guitar Institute of Technology in Hollywood, CA.
In his career he has performed with legendary musicians like James Moody, Claudio
Roditi, Ted Shumate, Jim Ates and Longeneu Parsons.
He has recorded eight projects and participated in many other albums.
During his performances on festivals in the Caribbean area, he discovered the beautiful sounds of the Steel Pan and incorporated it to his performances and recordings.
The Album Untitled Dreams was considered by critics as the
Venezuelan Jazz Recording of the Year.

There he studies trumpet with Egon Albrech, Music Theory with Violeta Lares
and Music History with
José Peñin. Under the direction of María Antonia Palacios, he becomes member of the
conservatory's orchestra and the wind ensemble. He participates in several
concerts playing baroque music, classical and contemporary, the latter under the
direction of composer Jackie Sheriber.
In 1985, Julio Mendoza's inclination for Jazz and popular music leads him to
spend time at nightclubs where this kind of music is played. He
starts working with singer Nancy Toro and becomes a member of several Jazz
bands. Playing with musicians such as Carlos Rojas, Víctor Mestas, Héctor
Hernández, Pedro López, Cristóbal Pitalúa, Roberto Jirón and Otmaro Ruiz.

Guitar

Biography
Marcos
Carrasco studied guitar with Gonzalo Micó from 1996 to 2001, took
advanced courses of Music at The ARS-NOVA school of Music, and attended
The Jazz Workshops of the JOSE REYNA CONSERVATORY.
He also took classes with Gerry Weil, Julio Mendoza, Julio Sanchez
and Alvaro Falcón, and attended Master Lectures from Paulo Bellinaty,
Tuck Andrews & Billy Sheehan.
Marcos
has played with musicians such as: Gonzalo Micó, Michael Berti, Marcus
Vinicius Da Fonseca, Junior Romero, Carlos Sanoja, Gerardo Chacón, Carlos
Rojas, Cristóbal Pitalúa and Heriberto Rojas among others.
Recently he participated in the FESTIVAL DE JAZZ DEL HATILLO.
The album JAZZ STANDARDS is his first commercial album, although he
previously recorded a promotional record called JAZZ TRIO with Giovanni
Ramirez and Willy Díaz.

Orlando Poleo - Bio & Discography
Orlando
Poleo
Born:
Resides:
Instrument s:

In
Caracas, Venezuela
Paris, France
Congas,

Jazz, Latin, Pop
Orlando was born in Caracas,
Venezuela where he began his musical training with the well-known teacher Julio Mendez.
He soon attracted attention and became one of the best and most demanded Venezuelan percussionists. He then studied Afro-Venezuelan percussion with teacher Miguel Urbina and later recorded and
went on to accompany many famous national and international artists. He also taught in various percussion schools in Venezuela.
In 1991 Orlando is invited to work in Paris where he finds lots of professional opportunities
consequently he then
spent
his time between Caracas and Paris. He makes his talents available to the best Latin artists of the Paris scene and to the Latin and jazz great names touring in France.
In 1995 he records his first album Cimarroneando in Caracas which he co-writes and co-arranges with the Cuban Orlando Maraca Valle (ex Irakere flautist).
Back in Paris, Orlando starts playing in all the famous Paris jazz clubs using 8 musicians among the best artists of the Paris Latin music scene. He names this group
CHAWORO
In 1997, back in Caracas to record his second album "EL BUEN CAMINO". The album is released in France in February 98.
Orlando tours intensively in France with his group "CHAWORO"
The end of 2001 is busy with the recording between Paris and Caracas of the third album "LO BUENO DE LA VIDA"

Sultanate of Oman. Cafe Paradiso, Amsterdam. Marciac Jazz Festival (France), Vannes Jazz Festival (France), Lisbon World Expo.

as: Birdland, Knitting Factory, Jazz Gallery, S.O.Bs, Kavehaz, Izzy Bar, etc.

-1988 Festival de Jazz de Caracas with Cimarron.

-1989 Festival de Jazz de Caracas, with Julio Mendozas Jazz Quintet.

Biography
Rodolfo Reyes
attended the most prestigious Music Schools of Venezuela until he
went to Boston and attended Berkley college of Music. Under the
schooling of Joseph Viola and John La Porta he graduated Magna Cum Laude
in 1983.
As a studio musician, Rodolfo has recorded with
many artists. His proficiency as
soloist in the jazz & Latin languages has led him play with some of
the best artists in the country and participate with them in different
jazz festivals worldwide.
His skills run so naturally that no matter if is
traditional, Latin, ballad,
free
or salsa, his performance
is always enjoyable.
Currently he is working as Producer and Musical Director of the band
Saxomania.
